description: Single-panel phase-fraction vs temperature plot (JMatPro 6.1 calculated) for the alloy Fe-6.57Al-3.3Mn-0.18C (wt.%). X-axis: "Temperature (°C)" from 0 to about 1550 (labelled ticks 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200, 1500); Y-axis: "Phase amount (wt.%)" from 0 to 100 (labelled ticks 0, 20, 40, 60, 80, 100). Four colour-coded curves are labelled directly on the plot: red "Ferrite", blue "Austenite", magenta "Carbides" and black "Liquid". Ferrite starts below the 100 wt.% gridline (between the 90 and 100 ticks) at 0 °C, stays essentially flat to roughly 600 °C, then shows a shallow dip to a minimum (near the 90 wt.% level) around 650-750 °C, and rises back to essentially 100 wt.% by about 1250 °C, remaining there until melting. Austenite is absent at low temperature, appears near 650-700 °C, rises to a peak of about 10 wt.% (first minor tick above zero), then decreases steadily and reaches zero at about 1250 °C. Carbides remain near zero (magenta, a few small bumps below ~2 wt.%). Liquid appears only as a steep black rise at about 1400 °C. The figure therefore demonstrates that this lean duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C alloy is ferrite-dominated, with an intercritical field in which austenite decreases and ferrite increases with rising temperature.

observations.observation: The plot has four labelled phase curves: red 'Ferrite', blue 'Austenite', magenta 'Carbides' and black 'Liquid'.
X-axis is labelled 'Temperature (°C)' with printed ticks at 0, 300, 600, 900, 1200 and 1500; y-axis is labelled 'Phase amount (wt.%)' with printed ticks at 0, 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100.
The ferrite curve remains above the 90 wt.% gridline over the whole temperature range up to melting, and returns to essentially 100 wt.% by about 1250 °C.
The ferrite curve shows a shallow minimum (curve body dropping to about the 90 wt.% gridline) in the roughly 650-750 °C window, coincident with the appearance of austenite.
Austenite is zero at low temperature, appears at about 650-700 °C, peaks at approximately 10 wt.% (near the first minor tick above zero), and falls to zero at about 1250 °C.
Carbides stay essentially at zero phase amount across the whole range, appearing only as small magenta bumps of a few wt.% or less.
Liquid fraction is zero until a steep black rise at about 1400 °C, indicating the solidus is close to that temperature.
The phase fractions were calculated with JMatPro 6.1 software (Sente Software, Ltd., Surrey, UK).
The plotted alloy composition is Fe-6.57Al-3.3Mn-0.18C (wt.%).

The citing text states that in the intercritical phase field the austenite (γ) content decreases and the ferrite (α) content increases with increasing temperature, in contrast to standard low-carbon steels.
The citing text describes the alloy as a lean duplex Fe-Mn-Al-C steel, consistent with the ferrite-dominant computed phase fractions.
